course_description:
Globally, telehealth is a popular, clinically effective communication vehicle that is rapidly becoming mainstream. This course introduces you to the key concepts relating to the use of telehealth to improve patient-centred clinical care. Course material covers the historical development of clinical telehealth in Australia and the contributions of other significant research innovators. A range of clinical telehealth applications will be explored using case examples that are relevant to today's health priority areas. You will review relevant guidelines and standards relating to telehealth integration and everyday practice of telehealth to provide equitable access to healthcare irrespective of the consumer's geographical location.

HLTH7113 is an introductory course in Clinical Telehealth. The focus of the course is on the use of telehealth, specifically in a clinical environment.

The course will:
course_aims: This course introduces you to the use of clinical telehealth as a means of delivering more equitable healthcare in areas where access to health services may be lacking. You will examine the types of equipment that can be used to perform telehealth, and learn about standards and guidelines to consider when conducting a telehealth consultation. The course covers aspects such as the history of telehealth, definitions and current applications and explores the privacy, security and medico-legal aspects that need to be considered.

learning_outcomes.description: Demonstrate an understanding of the concepts, theories, terminology and historical development of clinical telehealth.
Explain the different models and applications of clinical telehealth and their role within contemporary healthcare settings.
Analyse the role of clinical telehealth in improving healthcare access, equity and patient outcomes within Australian and global healthcare systems.

Apply evidence-based principles to the planning and delivery of safe, effective and patient centred clinical telehealth services, considering clinical, technological, organisational and patient factors.
Evaluate the privacy, security, ethical and medico legal considerations associated with clinical telehealth practice.
Communicate evidence informed recommendations relating to clinical telehealth using appropriate written and oral communication approaches for professional audiences.

assessment_details.title: Assessment Task 1: Clinical Telehealth Evaluation Report
assessment_details.task_description: Length: 1200-1500 words Purpose Clinical telehealth services vary considerably depending on the healthcare setting, patient population and clinical need. Evaluating existing telehealth models provides valuable insights into the factors that contribute to effective implementation and improved patient outcomes. For this assessment, you will compare one Australian and one international clinical telehealth service that address a similar healthcare need. Drawing on contemporary literature and evidence, you will evaluate the strengths and limitations of each service and identify evidence informed principles [SC1] that could guide future telehealth implementation. This assessment prepares you for Assessment Task 3, where you will apply these principles to recommend and justify a telehealth solution for a healthcare scenario. Part 1: Foundations of Clinical Telehealth (LO1) Approximately 250–300 words Provide an overview of clinical telehealth by: Defining clinical telehealth and introducing key concepts and terminology. Briefly describing the historical development of clinical telehealth. Explaining the growing role and importance of telehealth within contemporary healthcare. · Outline why you have chose the telehealth services you have – why the comparison Part 2: Comparative Evaluation of Two Clinical Telehealth Services (LO2) Select: One Australian clinical telehealth service. One international clinical telehealth service. The two services should address a similar healthcare need to enable meaningful comparison. A comparison table will be provided on Blackboard site. Part 3: Comparative Evaluation and Future Implementation (LO3) Approximately 700–900 words Drawing on your comparison and the contemporary literature, evaluate the two telehealth services by addressing the following: Compare the strengths and limitations of each telehealth service. Analyse how each service improves healthcare access, equity and patient outcomes. Evaluate the factors that appear to contribute most to the success of each service. Discuss the key similarities and differences between the two approaches. Drawing on the evidence from both services, identify three evidence informed implementation principles that should guide the design and implementation of future clinical telehealth services. Justify each implementation principle using evidence from your comparison and the contemporary literature. Examples of evidence informed implementation principles include: Designing telehealth services around the needs of the target patient population. Using hybrid models of care where clinically appropriate. Ensuring clinician training and organisational readiness prior to implementation. Addressing digital literacy and technology access to improve equity. Embedding strong privacy, security and governance practices. Evaluating telehealth services using patient outcomes and quality indicators to support continuous improvement. Submission Requirements Word limit: 1200–1500 words (excluding the comparison table and reference list). Submit one Word document containing: - Part 1: Foundations of clinicial telehealth - Part 2: Completed comparison table - Part 3: Comparative evaluation Reference list (APA 7th edition) Use APA 7th edition for in-text citations and the reference list. Support your discussion with peer-reviewed literature and government/policy documents. Write in formal academic language. Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.title: Assessment Task 3: Clinical Telehealth Implementation Proposal
assessment_details.task_description: Overview In this assessment, you will prepare and present a 8-10 minute PowerPoint presentation in which you recommend an appropriate telehealth solution for a healthcare service. You will be provided with a range of healthcare scenarios (available on Blackboard). Select one scenario and develop an evidence-based recommendation for the most appropriate telehealth solution to address the healthcare challenge presented. Imagine you have been engaged as a digital health consultant. Your role is to advise a healthcare organisation on the most appropriate telehealth solution for the scenario provided. Your recommendation should be evidence-based, practical, and tailored to the needs of the organisation and its patients. Your presentation should demonstrate how the proposed telehealth solution addresses the identified healthcare need while considering healthcare access, equity, patient outcomes, privacy, security and implementation issues. Your recommendation should be supported by current research evidence and relevant policy or professional guidance where appropriate. Presentation requirements - Prepared a 8-10 minute PowerPoint presentation. - Use PowerPoint slides effectively to communicate your ideas. Slides should support your presentation by using appropriate headings, diagrams, figures and limited text rather than large blocks of written content. - Present your ideas clearly and professionally using appropriate academic language. Healthcare scenarios will be available on Blackboard in the Assessment portal. Your presentation should address the following learning outcomes. 1. Healthcare Problem and Context (LO3) Analyse the healthcare problem described in your chosen scenario. Your discussion should include: · the nature and significance of the healthcare problem · the key stakeholders involved · barriers to healthcare access · equity considerations · the potential impact on patient outcomes Support your discussion with relevant evidence, statistics and literature. 2. Proposed Telehealth Solution (LO2 & LO3) Describe and justify the telehealth solution you recommend. Your discussion should include: · the telehealth modality (or combination of modalities) proposed · how the technology functions within the healthcare setting · why this solution is appropriate for the scenario · how it addresses the identified healthcare need Support your proposal with contemporary evidence and explain how the proposed solution aligns with safe, effective and patient centred telehealth practice. 3. Impact on Access, Equity and Patient Outcomes (LO3) Analyse the likely impact of the proposed telehealth solution. Your discussion should consider: · improvements in access to healthcare services · implications for health equity · effects on patient outcomes and quality of care · potential benefits for healthcare providers and the health system, where relevant Use contemporary evidence to support your analysis. 4. Privacy, Security and Medico-Legal Considerations (LO4) Evaluate the ethical, legal and professional considerations associated with implementing the proposed telehealth solution. Your discussion should include consideration of: · patient privacy and confidentiality · informed consent · data security and cybersecurity · professional responsibilities · relevant legal or regulatory issues · governance and risk mitigation strategies, potential risks and strategies to minimise them Apply evidence based principles to explain how the proposed telehealth solution could be implemented within the healthcare service. Consider clinical workflow, organisational readiness, workforce capability, technology and infrastructure requirements, patient readiness and digital literacy, as well as barriers and facilitators to successful implementation. 5. Evidence Informed Recommendations (LO4, 5 & 6) Provide evidence informed recommendations regarding the adoption and implementation of the proposed telehealth solution. Recommendations should be realistic, clearly justified and supported by the evidence presented throughout the presentation. The recommendations should identify: What should be done? Why should it be done? How should it be implemented? What needs to happen for it to succeed? How will success be evaluated? General Expectations Your presentation should: · demonstrate critical analysis rather than simply describing the telehealth technology · integrate evidence from peer-reviewed literature throughout the presentation · present a logical and well-structured argument · use APA 7th edition referencing for in-text citations and the reference list · communicate ideas clearly using professional presentation techniques and well-designed PowerPoint slides Read full task description Hide full task description

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 3 (27 Jul - 16 Aug)
learning_activities.topic: Module 1: Clinical telehealth - an overview Module 1 covers Weeks 1 - 3 of teaching. It offers a comprehensive understanding of telehealth, encompassing the definition of telehealth, tracing its historical origins and evolution into modern healthcare, and examining both initial and recent benefits. Module 1 explains how telehealth can increase (or reduce) access to healthcare for patients, with important considerations about equity in accessing telehealth and post-pandemic changes in Medicare Funding for telehealth. Week 1: What is Telehealth? Week 2: Telehealth - the past and the future Week 3: Benefits of telehealth Refer to the Course 'Learning Resources' on Learn.UQ for links to all lectures, Weekly Study Guide, required and recommended reading. Content is organised as Module and then by Teaching Week. Content is typically uploaded to Learn.UQ on the Friday prior to each Teaching Week. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 4 To Week 8 (17 Aug - 20 Sep)
learning_activities.topic: Module 2: Telehealth in action Teaching Weeks 4-8 explores the different telehealth approaches with respect to delivering healthcare i.e. store and forward models (i.e. asynchronous communication, secure messaging, encrypted software,) real-time models (i.e. synchronous communication - video or phone consultations), mobile health models (including remote monitoring/wearables) and hybrid models of care (i.e. a blend of telehealth modalities and/or face-to-face) Week 4: Approaches to telehealth - an overview Week 5: Telehealth in practice - real-time models Week 6: Telehealth in practice - store and forward models Week 7: Telehealth in practice - mobile health models Week 8: Telehealth in practice - hybrid models of care Refer to the Course 'Learning Resources' on Learn.UQ for links to all lectures, Weekly Study Guide, required and recommended reading. Content is organised as Module and then by Teaching Week. Content is typically uploaded to Learn.UQ on the Friday prior to each Teaching Week.

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 9 To Week 13 (21 Sep - 01 Nov)
learning_activities.topic: Module 3: Planning & implenting telehealth Teaching Weeks 9-12 outlines practical considerations, technical requirements, planning for a telehealth program or a telehealth consultation and privacy and sustainability considerations. Week 13 is reserved for review of key concepts covered over the semester that will assist you with the final assessment. Week 9: Planning for telehealth Week 10: Privacy considerations and sustainability of telehealth Week 11: Telehealth - future potential Week 12: Telehealth - a global perspective Week 13: Review Refer to the Course 'Learning Resources' on Learn.UQ for links to all lectures, Weekly Study Guide, required and recommended reading. Weeks 9-12 content will be available from Teaching Week 9 to assist you with final assessment preparation.
